summary.oneLiner: Ashram Online.com Limited is a BSE-listed Chennai-based trading and e-commerce company selling traditional and spiritual products and pooja services across India.
summary.business: Ashram Online.com Limited (formerly Tatia Skylines and Health Farms Limited), incorporated in 1991, is engaged in the trading and marketing of a diverse range of traditional and spiritual products, including sacred threads, pooja accessories, ritual essentials and other heritage-inspired offerings. It also provides homam and pooja services. The Company leverages digital platforms and modern distribution channels to make its products and services accessible to customers across India, and states it is engaged in the business of e-commerce with no manufacturing facility or plant.

endMarkets: Retail customers across India|Digital / e-commerce platforms and modern distribution channels

currentContext.expansion: Ashram Online.com Limited is an asset-light, service-and-trading business: the Corporate Governance report states the Company is engaged in the business of e-commerce and does not have any manufacturing facility or plant. The MD&A describes expansion only in footprint and service terms — the Company delivers Homam, Puja, Pariharam and Samskaram ceremonies through technology-enabled platforms to devotees across India and overseas, and 'remains focused on strengthening its service offerings, expanding its customer reach and improving operational efficiency to support sustainable growth.' Among stated opportunities are the expansion of digital platforms enabling wider customer outreach and service accessibility, and opportunities to introduce new value-added spiritual services and enhance customer engagement. No capacity addition, project, commissioning timeline, new site or acquisition is disclosed, and no rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in the routed material.

risks.note: The MD&A lists 'Slowdown in economic activity affecting discretionary consumer spending' as a threat. Online homam, puja, pariharam and samskaram services are wholly discretionary purchases, so demand tracks household sentiment rather than any contracted revenue base.

risks.risk: Competition from organised and unorganised service providers
risks.note: Explicitly flagged in the MD&A. The offering has no disclosed patent, certification or exclusive supply arrangement, and the barriers to a competing devotional-services platform or a local temple/priest network are low.
The MD&A flags 'Changes in applicable laws, regulations and taxation policies that may affect business operations' — relevant for a GST-rated services and goods-trading model delivered online.

The MD&A flags 'Technology-related risks, including cybersecurity, data privacy and uninterrupted platform availability'. The entire delivery model is technology-enabled, so a platform outage or data-privacy incident is an operating risk, not merely an IT one.

The MD&A states the Company 'presently operates in a single business segment' so separate segment-wise reporting is not applicable. There is no diversification to absorb a downturn in devotional-services demand, and the Company has no manufacturing facility or plant of its own.

risks.risk: Balance-sheet concentration in demand loans to related parties
risks.note: The auditor's CARO annexure records that loans and advances in the nature of loans are repayable on demand or carry no stipulated terms of repayment, with the great majority extended to related parties; it also notes that for the unsecured loans given, repayment of principal and payment of interest have not been stipulated and the Company has not demanded repayment during the year. The Related Party note lists Kreon Finnancial Services Ltd, Tatia Global Vennture Limited and Opti Products Private Limited as enterprises over which KMP exercise significant influence, and as counterparties to those loans — so recoverability depends on entities under common influence rather than arm's-length borrowers.

The MD&A states the Company recorded a net loss in FY2025-26 against a net loss in the previous financial year, and the CARO annexure reports cash losses in both the year under audit and the immediately preceding year. Sustained cash losses at this scale make the business dependent on its investment/loan book and on promoter borrowings rather than on operating cash generation.

risks.risk: Long-standing disputed income-tax demands before the Madras High Court
risks.note: The CARO annexure discloses income tax and interest demands for assessment years 1994-95 and 1995-96 that have not been deposited on account of dispute and remain pending before the Madras High Court — an unresolved contingent exposure carried for roughly three decades.

The Company had only four permanent employees on its rolls as at 31 March 2026 and is run by a single Whole-time Director who is also Chairperson. The Founder Director died during/after the year (ceased 29/04/2026) and the Company Secretary changed mid-year, so execution, compliance and continuity rest on very few individuals.

risks.risk: Equity price and credit risk on a financial-asset-heavy balance sheet
risks.note: The financial-instruments note states the Company holds quoted equity investments and is exposed to changes in market prices, and that credit risk arises from trade receivables from corporate customers. For a business whose assets are largely investments, loans and other financial assets, market and counterparty movements drive reported results as much as trading operations do.
